Outbreak probabilities for a spatial branching process

Source: R/core.R
outbreak_prob.Rd

Computes the maximal fixed point of the multitype branching-process equations in Wang and Valdano (2026), using the convention that rows of R are destinations and columns are sources. Iteration starts at a vector of ones. The Poisson calculation uses -expm1(-crossprod(R, p)). The negative-binomial calculation implements Eq. (5) with log1p() and expm1() for numerical stability.

Usage

outbreak_prob(
  R,
  tol = 1e-12,
  max_iter = 1e+05,
  offspring = "poisson",
  omega = 0
)

Arguments

R

A finite, nonnegative square reproduction matrix. R[i, j] is the expected number of infections in destination i caused by one infected individual from source j.

tol

Positive convergence tolerance for both the iteration change and fixed-point residual.

max_iter

Positive integer giving the maximum number of iterations.

offspring

Offspring distribution. Either "poisson" (the default) or "nb" for independent negative-binomial counts on directed edges.

omega

A finite nonnegative scalar overdispersion parameter. For the negative-binomial model, size = 1 / omega and Var(X[i,j]) = R[i,j] * (1 + omega * R[i,j]). The value zero recovers the Poisson model. Heterogeneous dispersion matrices are unsupported.

Value

A named numeric vector, indexed by source community.

Details

In subcritical and critical regimes, the theoretically correct maximal fixed point is zero. The function returns it directly when the spectral radius is at or below one (within a relative numerical tolerance), avoiding arbitrarily slow convergence near the threshold. Above the threshold, monotone iteration is supplemented by safeguarded Newton steps when useful; the fixed-point residual is still checked before a result is returned.

Examples

R <- matrix(c(1.2, 0.2, 0.3, 0.8), 2, byrow = TRUE,
            dimnames = list(c("A", "B"), c("A", "B")))
outbreak_prob(R)
#>         A         B 
#> 0.4826325 0.2661426
